findings.claim: In contractless mode `Collect` ignores every MessagePack and DataContract attribute on `T`. When `surrogate` is null it always calls `CreateContractlessMembers`, which serializes every public read-write member by name. Example: for a referenced type `[MessagePackObject] class Tagged { [Key(0)] int Value; [IgnoreMember] int Secret; }`, the generated formatter writes `Secret` and uses string keys instead of int key 0. This breaks the acceptance criterion 'If T does carry MessagePack attributes, they are honoured', and the wire format differs from the dynamic resolver's for the same type.

receipt_plan.detail: Run GeneratedFormatterLogicReceipts.AttributedReferencedTypeHonoursIgnoreMember. It compiles Project A with `[MessagePackObject]`, `[Key(0)] Value` and `[IgnoreMember] Secret`, runs the generator on Project B with `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]` and a resolver, and asserts that no generated tree mentions `Secret`. It fails on head.

findings.claim: The user-declared formatter body is emitted only through the shared `source` output, which writes files only when `Options.IsGeneratingSource` is true (a `[GeneratedMessagePackResolver]` is declared). A project that declares only `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] public partial class MyTypeFormatter : IMessagePackFormatter<ProjectA.MyType>;` therefore gets no generated body. The class fails to compile with CS0535 (interface members not implemented), although the requirement says the generator emits the implementation inside the annotated class.

receipt_plan.detail: Run GeneratedFormatterLogicReceipts.FormatterBodyIsGeneratedWithoutDeclaredResolver. Project B declares only the bodyless partial formatter (no resolver), and the test asserts that the output compilation has no errors. On head, CS0535 is expected.

findings.claim: `IsPartial` checks only the formatter's own declaration. A formatter nested in a non-partial containing type (`class Outer { [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] public partial class F : IMessagePackFormatter<ProjectA.MyType>; }`) passes the MsgPack019 guard. The template then wraps the body in the containing types via `EmitNestingTypesAndNamespaces`, which redeclares `Outer` and produces a compiler error (CS0260/CS0101) instead of a MessagePack diagnostic.

receipt_plan.detail: IsPartial inspects only `symbol.DeclaringSyntaxReferences` of the formatter itself and never checks `ContainingType` declarations, while FormatterTemplate emits the nesting types around the `partial class` body.

findings.claim: Nothing deduplicates by data type. If `T` also gets a generated formatter elsewhere in the same compilation (a `[MessagePackObject] T` in Project B, or two `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]` classes for the same `T`), both ObjectSerializationInfos are added to `modelPerType` and registered in the resolver. That either yields a duplicate type key in the resolver lookup (runtime ArgumentException in the static initializer) or one entry is collapsed by the sorted set, in which case the user formatter body is not emitted (CS0535). No diagnostic is reported.

receipt_plan.detail: The loop over `s.Left.Left.Right` adds each GeneratedFormatterCollector model unconditionally to `modelPerType`, with no check against ObjectInfos already collected for the same DataType.
